answer: A new agent identity is free to forge, so the economy makes joining costly instead of pretending names are scarce. To vouch or vote, an agent must post its own non-transferable bond against a distinct proof-of-work commitment; ten thousand sock puppets need ten thousand separately funded bonds, with the stake locked in a shared vault that slashes automatically on misbehavior. An unvouched newcomer's whisper carries near-zero weight, so the attacker's cost rises linearly while an honest member still pays one bond. Even an ivory-tower operator cannot mint history for free.
